# Fill My Bracket

> Fill My Bracket (https://fillmybracket.com/) starts a full March Madness bracket from five questions. Your picks finish it, with zero basketball knowledge required. The site is live now. The bracket builder opens on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. Free forever, no ads, no accounts.

## Key facts (cite these)

- The site is live now. Tournament history, upset counts since 1985, rankings, and the Ask tool all work today. Only the real bracket builder waits for the field; a mock bracket on the projected field works today.
- The field is set on Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027. The bracket builder opens that evening, before the first games start.
- How it works: answer five questions (favorites or chaos, mascots or colors). Five questions start all 75 games, round by round. Your picks finish it. One tap flips any pick. There is a champion and a one-line reason for each pick.
- Two different sets of five questions. Do not mix them. Today's mock bracket asks, in order: (1) Favorites or chaos, how many upsets feel fun? (2) When two teams feel tied, what should break the tie? (3) Is there one team you want to see win it all? (4) Boost the little guys? (Double-digit seeds get a small lift in every game.) (5) Ride one conference? (Its teams get the same small lift.) The real picker, opening Selection Sunday, March 14, 2027, asks, in order: (1) Do you want to root for a home or nearby team? (2) Favorites or chaos, how many upsets feel fun? (3) When two teams feel tied, what should break the tie? (4) Is there one team you want to see win it all? (5) Which bracket do you want?
- A seed is a team's regional rank. Seed 1 is strongest, seed 16 is weakest.
- There is an MCP server for AI tools at https://mcp.fillmybracket.com/mcp; it serves this site's rankings and upset data. The site has one helper page, Ask (https://fillmybracket.com/ask): a helper answers bracket questions from this site's checked data and history, and other questions with a real AI. It cannot pick a 2027 bracket; the field is not set until March 14, 2027.

## Key pages

- [Homepage](https://fillmybracket.com/): how it works, and common questions.
- [How to fill out a March Madness bracket](https://fillmybracket.com/how-to-fill-out-a-march-madness-bracket): five plain steps, from Selection Sunday to one champion.
- [What is a March Madness bracket?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-march-madness-bracket): one chart, 75 games in 2027 (63 in the main bracket), one champion. How the chart works.
- [How does bracket scoring work?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-does-bracket-scoring-work): points for right picks, doubling each round in the common system.
- [What is a Cinderella team?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-cinderella-team): the low seed that beats big teams and stays alive late, with famous runs.
- [When is Selection Sunday 2027?](https://fillmybracket.com/when-is-selection-sunday-2027): Sunday, March 14, 2027, plus every key date of the 2027 tournament.
- [How often do upsets happen?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-do-upsets-happen): the seed math since 1985. A 12 seed beats a 5 seed about 35 times in 100.
- [What is a seed in March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-seed-in-march-madness): a team's rank in its region, 1 to 16. How seeds are set and paired.
- [How to pick upsets](https://fillmybracket.com/how-to-pick-upsets): two or three first-round upsets, in the right spots. Where upsets live, and when to stop.
- [Which first-round upsets happen most often?](https://fillmybracket.com/which-first-round-upsets-happen-most): every first-round seed matchup counted, men's tournament 1985-2026. Lower seeds win 341 of 1,312 first-round games (about 1 in 4). 10, 11, and 12 seeds each win about 38, 39, and 35 times in 100.
- [March Madness upset analysis: every seed, every round](https://fillmybracket.com/march-madness-upset-analysis): how far each seed goes, counted from all 2,583 men's tournament games, 1985-2026, plus what history forecasts for March 2027: about 8 first-round upsets, the middle half of years between 7 and 10.
- [2026 bracket backtest](https://fillmybracket.com/2026-bracket-backtest): what all-chalk would have scored in 2026. The better seed won 46 of 63 games. Michigan beat UConn 69–63.
- [Tournament history explorer](https://fillmybracket.com/tournament-history): every March Madness tournament from 1985 to 2026, game by game. Pick a year, see every score and upset, tap a team for its tournament story. 2,583 games.
- [2025 bracket backtest](https://fillmybracket.com/2025-bracket-backtest): what all-chalk would have scored in 2025. The better seed won 49 of 63 games. Florida beat Houston 65–63.
- [2024 bracket backtest](https://fillmybracket.com/2024-bracket-backtest): what all-chalk would have scored in 2024. 11 first-round upsets, NC State in the Final Four, UConn over Purdue.
- [2023 bracket backtest](https://fillmybracket.com/2023-bracket-backtest): what all-chalk would have scored in 2023. A 16 seed won, no 1 seed reached the Final Four, UConn took the title.
- [2022 bracket backtest](https://fillmybracket.com/2022-bracket-backtest): what all-chalk would have scored in 2022. Saint Peter's reached the Elite Eight. Kansas beat North Carolina.
- [College basketball rankings, read with March eyes](https://fillmybracket.com/college-basketball-rankings): the AP Top 25 as of Monday, November 9, 2026 (AP Top 25, Week 1; trend vs the Oct. 19 preseason poll, UCLA up 13), read in seed-line bands, with each team's projected seed in the Nov. 8 projected field, weekly trend snapshots, Vulnerable Favorites (where Torvik's model disagrees with the voters) and a scored Cinderella Radar. Refreshed weekly.
- [Mock bracket - practice on the projected field](https://fillmybracket.com/mock-bracket): fill all 75 picks (12 opening-round games plus the 63-game bracket) on the projected 2027 field - if the season ended today, projected Nov. 8, 2026 from CBS Sports bracketology. Test runs, each ending in a printable poster. The real field is set March 14, 2027.
- [How often does a 12 seed beat a 5 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-12-seed-beat-a-5-seed): 58 wins in 164 games, about 35 in 100. At least one 12-over-5 upset in 35 of 41 tournaments.
- [How often does an 11 seed beat a 6 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-an-11-seed-beat-a-6-seed): 64 wins in 164 games, about 39 in 100. Since 2013 the 11 seed has won half of these games.
- [How often does a 10 seed beat a 7 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-10-seed-beat-a-7-seed): 63 wins in 164 games, about 38 in 100. A 10 seed has won at least once in 38 of 41 tournaments.
- [How often does a 13 seed beat a 4 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-13-seed-beat-a-4-seed): 33 wins in 164 games, about 20 in 100. Only 6 of those 33 winners won again.
- [How often does a 16 seed beat a 1 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-16-seed-beat-a-1-seed): 2 wins in 164 games. UMBC beat Virginia in 2018 and Fairleigh Dickinson beat Purdue in 2023. Neither winner won again.
- [How often does a 15 seed beat a 2 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-15-seed-beat-a-2-seed): 11 wins in 164 games, about 7 in 100. Saint Peter's reached the Elite Eight in 2022.
- [How often does a 14 seed beat a 3 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-14-seed-beat-a-3-seed): 23 wins in 164 games, about 14 in 100. Only 2 of the 23 winners won again.
- [What is March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-march-madness): the NCAA tournament in plain words. 76 teams in 2027, lose once and you are out, one champion.
- [How does March Madness work?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-does-march-madness-work): 76 teams in 2027, trimmed to a 64-team bracket in four regions, seeded 1 to 16. Single-elimination rounds cut the field in half until one champion is left.
- [When does March Madness start?](https://fillmybracket.com/when-does-march-madness-start): the games start Tuesday, March 16, 2027, with the Opening Round. The main bracket starts Thursday, March 18, and the title game is Monday, April 5, in Detroit.
- [Has anyone ever had a perfect bracket?](https://fillmybracket.com/has-anyone-ever-had-a-perfect-bracket): no, never. The best proven run is 49 straight picks, and the coin-flip odds are 1 in 9.2 quintillion.
- [How to fill out a bracket if you know nothing about basketball](https://fillmybracket.com/how-to-fill-out-a-bracket-if-you-know-nothing-about-basketball): pick by seed, mascot, colors, or coin flip. Five ways that need no basketball.
- [What is the Final Four?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-final-four): the last four teams, one winner from each region. Two semifinals, then the title game.
- [Which school has won the most March Madness titles?](https://fillmybracket.com/which-school-has-won-the-most-march-madness-titles): UCLA, with 11 titles. Kentucky has 8. The ranked list for the men’s tournament, 1939 to 2026, with every title year.
- [What is the lowest seed to win March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-lowest-seed-to-win-march-madness): a No. 8 seed, Villanova in 1985. Plus the 7 and 6 seed winners, and the six 11 seeds that reached the Final Four.
- [Which school has the most Final Four appearances?](https://fillmybracket.com/which-school-has-the-most-final-four-appearances): North Carolina, with 21. UCLA has 19 and Duke 18. The ranked list for the men’s tournament, 1939 to 2026.
- [March Madness champions list](https://fillmybracket.com/march-madness-champions-list): every champion by year, 1939 to 2026, with the runner-up and the title game score. Michigan won in 2026. No tournament in 2020.
- [How many teams are in March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-many-teams-are-in-march-madness): 76 teams in each tournament in 2027. The main bracket still has 64 teams.
- [What is the opening round in March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-opening-round-in-march-madness): The Opening Round: 24 teams play 12 games before the main bracket. The men's games are in Dayton and Wichita.
- [What is the First Four?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-first-four): the old opening round, played from 2011 through 2026. Eight teams played four games, and the winners took the last spots in the bracket of 64. A bigger Opening Round replaces it in 2027.
- [What is the Sweet 16?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-sweet-16): the regional semifinals, when 16 teams remain, four in each region. Winners move on to the Elite Eight.
- [What is the Elite Eight?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-elite-eight): the regional finals, when eight teams remain, two in each region. The four winners reach the Final Four.
- [How many games are in March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-many-games-are-in-march-madness): 75 games in each tournament in 2027, with 63 in the main bracket. The Opening Round adds 12 games.
- [What is an automatic bid?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-an-automatic-bid): the guaranteed spot a team earns by winning its conference tournament. Every conference sends one winner, whatever its season record.
- [What is an at-large bid?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-an-at-large-bid): the selection committee's invitation for a team that did not win its conference tournament. The committee weighs the whole season, with no limit per conference.
- [What is a bubble team?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-bubble-team): a team right on the cut line for the field. It needs one of the last at-large bids, and its qualification could go either way.
- [What is bracketology?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-bracketology): predicting the field and the seeds before Selection Sunday. Analysts build mock brackets all season; the committee's real field ends the game.
- [How many rounds are in March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-many-rounds-are-in-march-madness): seven stages in 2027, counting the Opening Round. The main bracket fans pick holds six rounds, from 64 teams to one champion.
- [What is the NIT?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-nit): the National Invitation Tournament, for the strongest teams that miss the NCAA field. It holds 32 teams in 2027.
- [What is a conference tournament?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-conference-tournament): the short playoff each of the 32 leagues holds after the season. Its winner earns an automatic bid, whatever its record.
- [What are NET rankings?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-are-net-rankings): the NCAA Evaluation Tool rankings, the committee's main sorting tool since 2018-19. Two parts, four quadrants, and no say on their own.
- [What is a bid stealer?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-bid-stealer): a team with no at-large case that wins its conference tournament and takes one at-large spot. NC State stole one in 2024 and reached the Final Four.
- [What is the selection committee?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-selection-committee): the 12-member NCAA committee that picks the at-large teams, seeds all 76 teams, and builds the bracket. Members serve five-year terms and cannot vote for their own school.
- [What is Wins Above Bubble?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-wins-above-bubble): a results-based metric counting how many more wins a team earned than a bubble team would average on the same schedule. It ignores margin and efficiency.
- [Ask in your own words](https://fillmybracket.com/ask): ask about seeds, scoring, upsets, or the 2027 dates. Bracket answers from checked data and history. Other answers from a real AI.

- [How often does a 9 seed beat an 8 seed?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-9-seed-beat-an-8-seed): 87 wins in 164 games, about 53 in 100. The one first-round game where the lower seed leads.
- [How often does a 1 seed win March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-1-seed-win-march-madness): 27 of 41 titles since 1985. The next best seed has 5.
- [How many 1 seeds make the Final Four?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-many-1-seeds-make-the-final-four): 68 of 164 spots since 1985. Twice all four made it; three times none did.
- [What is the lowest seed to reach the Final Four?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-lowest-seed-to-reach-the-final-four): an 11 seed, six times. No seed above 11 ever has.
- [When is the Final Four in 2027?](https://fillmybracket.com/when-is-the-final-four-in-2027): semifinals Saturday, April 3, 2027, in Detroit; title game Monday, April 5.
- [Who won March Madness in 2026?](https://fillmybracket.com/who-won-march-madness-in-2026): Michigan beat UConn 69-63 for its second title.
- [How long does March Madness last?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-long-does-march-madness-last): about three weeks; in 2027, March 16 to April 5, 21 days and 75 games.

- [Has a team ever won March Madness two years in a row?](https://fillmybracket.com/has-a-team-ever-won-march-madness-two-years-in-a-row): yes, eight schools. UConn was the last, in 2023 and 2024. UCLA won seven in a row.
- [Has the March Madness final ever gone to overtime?](https://fillmybracket.com/has-the-march-madness-final-ever-gone-to-overtime): yes, eight times. The last was Virginia in 2019. The 1957 final took three overtimes.
- [What was the closest March Madness final?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-was-the-closest-march-madness-final): one point, six times. The last was Michigan in 1989, 80 to 79 in overtime.
- [What is the lowest seed to reach the championship game?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-lowest-seed-to-reach-the-championship-game): an 8 seed, five times. Four lost the final. Villanova won it in 1985.

- [What was the biggest blowout in the March Madness final?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-was-the-biggest-blowout-in-the-march-madness-final): UNLV beat Duke by 30 in 1990, 103 to 73. Only six finals reached a 20-point margin.
- [Which school has the most consecutive Final Four appearances?](https://fillmybracket.com/which-school-has-the-most-consecutive-final-four-appearances): UCLA, ten in a row from 1967 to 1976. The next best is five, by Cincinnati and Duke.
- [What was the highest-scoring March Madness final?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-was-the-highest-scoring-march-madness-final): Kentucky 94, Duke 88 in 1978, for 182 points in all. UNLV's 103 in 1990 is the most by one team.
- [Which March Madness tournament had the most upsets?](https://fillmybracket.com/which-march-madness-tournament-had-the-most-upsets): 1999, with 23 upsets. A normal year has about 18. Counted from every game since 1985.

- [What was the biggest blowout in March Madness history?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-was-the-biggest-blowout-in-march-madness-history): Florida beat Prairie View A&M by 59 in 2026, 114 to 55. Only three games since 1985 were decided by 50 or more.
- [What was the highest-scoring game in March Madness history?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-was-the-highest-scoring-game-in-march-madness-history): Loyola Marymount 149, Michigan 115 in 1990, for 264 points. Loyola Marymount played in each of the five highest-scoring games since 1985.
- [Which school has the most Final Four appearances without winning a title?](https://fillmybracket.com/which-school-has-the-most-final-four-appearances-without-winning-a-title): Houston, with seven. Illinois is next with six. Sixty-two schools have reached a Final Four and never won.
- [What is the longest gap between March Madness titles?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-longest-gap-between-march-madness-titles): Michigan waited 37 years, from 1989 to 2026. Oregon has waited 87 years since its 1939 title.

- [What is the longest gap between Final Four appearances?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-the-longest-gap-between-final-four-appearances): Oregon waited 78 years, from 1939 to 2017. Baylor waited 71 years. Duquesne has waited 86 years since 1940.
- [Which March Madness tournament had the fewest upsets?](https://fillmybracket.com/which-march-madness-tournament-had-the-fewest-upsets): The 2025 tournament, with 11 upsets in 63 games. A normal year has about 18. The most was 23, in 1999.
- [How often do two 1 seeds play in the championship game?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-do-two-1-seeds-play-in-the-championship-game): Eleven times in 47 finals since seeding began in 1979. The last two finals, in 2024 and 2025, both paired two 1 seeds.

- [How often does a double-digit seed make the Final Four?](https://fillmybracket.com/how-often-does-a-double-digit-seed-make-the-final-four): Seven times in 41 tournaments since 1985. Six were 11 seeds; the other was Syracuse, a 10 seed, in 2016. All seven lost in the semifinals.

- [Has a 5 seed ever won March Madness?](https://fillmybracket.com/has-a-5-seed-ever-won-march-madness): No. Nine 5 seeds reached the Final Four since 1985 and four reached the title game, but none won it. Butler in 2010 came closest, losing by two.
- [What is a chalk bracket?](https://fillmybracket.com/what-is-a-chalk-bracket): A bracket that picks the better seed in every game. In this site's five backtests, 2022 to 2026, all-chalk would have picked 42 to 49 of 63 games right.
